name: Jerimoth
overview: Jerimoth was a male figure identified uniquely as a son of King David, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 11:18. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention in Scripture is brief but establishes his place within the royal lineage of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jerimoth is a proper name meaning 'swollen or obese.' This meaning is noted but not indicated as being given directly by God. It reflects the Hebrew linguistic background of the name as found in 2 Chronicles 11:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jerimoth as a son of David. It is also inferred that Mahalath was his mother, based on the same passage in 2 Chronicles 11:18. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jerimoth's significance lies primarily in his identification as a son of David, linking him to the Messianic lineage through which God's covenant promises were fulfilled. Although his role is not elaborated upon, his inclusion in the genealogical records underscores the importance of David's descendants in God's unfolding plan. This connection invites reflection on the faithfulness of God's promises through the Davidic line.
